title: Fair ASR: Re-Evaluating Black-Box Jailbreaks under Shared Target-Call Budgets
abstract: arXiv:2608.17360v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Reliable jailbreak evaluation is essential for assessing LLM safety, but most existing studies rely solely on attack success rate (ASR) without accounting for its dependence on attack budgets, resulting in unfair comparisons across methods. Existing compute-aware evaluations reduce heterogeneous resources into FLOPs, which is difficult to estimate for black-box models and fails to capture resource-specific constraints. To provide a comparable evaluation basis, we introduce Fair-ASR, an evaluation protocol for black-box jailbreak attacks under shared target-call budgets B, using target calls as a directly observable and method-agnostic comparison axis while tracking attacker calls separately for efficiency analysis. translated_title: 公平ASR：在共享目标调用预算下重新评估黑盒越狱攻击
translated_abstract: 可靠的越狱评估对于评估大型语言模型的安全性至关重要，但大多数现有研究仅依赖攻击成功率（ASR），未考虑其对攻击预算的依赖性，导致不同方法之间的比较不公平。现有的计算感知评估将异构资源简化为浮点运算次数（FLOPs），这对黑盒模型难以估计，且无法捕捉特定资源的约束。为了提供可比较的评估基础，我们引入了公平ASR（Fair-ASR），这是一种在共享目标调用预算B下的黑盒越狱攻击评估协议，使用目标调用作为直接可观察且与方法无关的比较轴，同时单独跟踪攻击者调用以进行效率分析。我们在公平ASR协议下重新评估了11种代表性攻击，发现攻击排名在目标调用预算上发生显著变化，简单的随机扰动和手工设计的模板仍具有高度竞争力。
tldr: 提出了公平ASR评估协议，以共享目标调用预算为基准重新评估黑盒越狱攻击，发现攻击排名随预算变化且简单方法仍具竞争力。
en_tdlr: We propose Fair-ASR, an evaluation protocol using shared target-call budgets to re-assess black-box jailbreak attacks, revealing that attack rankings shift across budgets and simple methods remain competitive.
